agreed.medi_said: Do you guys use enough كافية? Is, uh، is this an Arabic word or no?
agreed.why: He asked whether كافية is used; Amal supplied بكفي - a didn't-know.

agreed.medi_said: Yeah، راح يسعد. Yeah، راح يسعدني. [unintelligible] It
agreed.why: يسعد means make happy; he meant 'it will help (me)' and Amal gave يساعد. (He self-fixed أسعدني to يسعدني before her; the fixed version is what she corrected.)

agreed.medi_said: بفكر إنه كل إشي بيحر-- كل إشي بيحر-- بيحرك.
agreed.amal_said: بيت حرك. ... لا، بيت is you getting moved. So كل إشي gets moved.
agreed.why: بيحرك = moves something; for 'everything is moving' Amal gave بيتحرك and explained the t- form is getting moved.
agreed.english: I think everything is moving (so fast).

agreed.why: He meant 'do you like the rain?' (she just said it was nice); بدك = want. She answered with بحب and he took it ('بـ-بتحب، yeah').

agreed.medi_said: أنا جربت بس الـ set، uh, يخرب، uh, يخرب-- يخرب-- يخرب؟
agreed.why: Telling what happened (the card set broke) needs past; he said present يخرب and asked, Amal gave past خربه; he then said خربوا 'That's right'.
agreed.english: I tried, but the set broke (it).

agreed.medi_said: بنت به. Uh, بنت به. Yeah, بنت, بنت به is to, to take care of something.
agreed.amal_said: Actually، بنتبه is more like pay attention.
agreed.right: بنتبه = pay attention (ديري بالك = take care)
agreed.why: Asked for 'pay attention' vs 'take care', he gave انتبه for take care; Amal said it means pay attention and he said 'Oh, whoops'.
agreed.english: Which word means take care / pay attention.

agreed.medi_said: أنا لازم أتدرب، uh, ستي ... بتدرب لا؟
agreed.amal_said: وبتدرب شو، شو بتدرب بتاخد؟ ... A preposition. ... على.
agreed.why: He left out the preposition after أتدرب; Amal prompted ('A preposition'), he guessed لا, and she supplied على.
agreed.english: I have to practice the set.

agreed.why: She asked for a command; he said a past-tense 'you (f) exercised' form, Amal said 'أمر' (command) and he changed to تمارني.

agreed.medi_said: بيجيب اللي. ... بيجيب اللي أي. Yeah.
agreed.amal_said: جبيلي إياه. Why did you put be؟
agreed.why: A command has no b-; Amal gave جيبلي إياه and asked why he put the b-.
'Fool someone' is ضحك على; he said hadeekna (made us laugh) and Amal repeated ضحك until he said tehekalayna.

agreed.medi_said: Hadik al-dawla, uh, is, uh, biddik jibal.
agreed.why: 'If you like mountains' came without el-; Amal recast الجبال (and confirmed plural جبال, singular جبل). He asked 'what did I say?'.

agreed.medi_said: Surprise. It's, uh, I don't know how to say surprise.
agreed.why: He said he did not know 'surprise'; Amal supplied مفاجأة.
agreed.english: Keep quiet about the party because it's a surprise.

agreed.medi_said: Because you forgot your keys, so ashan nisti ma-- uh... But what is it for you feminine? Is it nisti?
agreed.amal_said: Mm. So you forgot. It's one of the irregulars. ... Nseeti because, because you is nseed.
agreed.why: Past 'you (f) forgot' is irregular نسيتي; he used nisti in his sentence and Amal gave nseeti, which he repeated.

agreed.medi_said: حوالي، uh, تيس-- ... Would I say تيس على تيس؟
agreed.why: Clock time needs el- (على التسع); he said تيس bare and Amal recast twice, he repeated على التيس.

agreed.medi_said: [speaking foreign language] على. And that one is logical.
agreed.why: 'Keep quiet about' is اسكت عن; he gave على and Amal said عن.
For 'scare me' he used khafi (get scared); Amal said 'No' and he moved to the doubled-middle خوفني.

r1.why: He knows the verb (sheet: 'i remove / take away | Ana ba2eem | أنا بقيم') but guessed a wrong past form; Amal gave إمت (2ayyamt) and بقيم and he took it ('بعيم, that's right. So إمت').

r2.why: He asked how to say 'I removed (the apps)' and offered بعيد (far); Amal answered with إمت (her word as the engine wrote it) and used it again at 05:06 'لما إمت الـ Instagram'.
r2.english: I removed / deleted Instagram and the games

r1.medi_said: اليوم أنا إمت، uh, Instagram و لوب، uh، ألعاب، uh، من تلفوني
r1.why: Specific games he deleted from his phone need el-; Amal later (05:06) says 'إمت الـ Instagram والـ ألعاب' but that is two minutes later, so treated as let-pass.
r1.english: Today I removed Instagram and the games from my phone.

r1.medi_said: Ah، بكافية، okay. Uh، كل، كل اليوم مش-- uh، ما عندي بكافية وقت.
r1.why: He means 'every day I don't have enough time'; kul + el- = the whole day, every day is كل يوم. Amal did not react.
r1.english: Every day I don't have enough time.

r2.medi_said: كل اليوم مش-- uh، ما عندي بكافية وقت.
r2.why: The adjective goes after its noun (وقت بكفي); Amal re-said it in that order.

r1.why: The 'enough' word goes after the noun (وقت بكفي); Amal's reply puts it after وقت. Same moment as the vocab row.

r1.why: For weather 'in between' Amal echoed بينهم then gave نص نص, which he repeated; may be her offering an alternative, so low.

r2.why: He reached for 'in between' (neither cold nor hot) with بينهم; Amal confirmed it and supplied نص نص, which he repeated. Help on the way, so low.
